title: Designing Network Design Spaces
authors: Ilija Radosavovic, Raj Prateek Kosaraju, Ross Girshick, Kaiming He, Piotr Dollár
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
conclusions: Proposes 'design space design': instead of hand-designing or NAS-searching a single best network instance, design a population-level parametrized space of networks and analyze it via error empirical-distribution-function (EDF) statistics over sampled models.

Progressively simplifies an unconstrained AnyNet design space (via shared bottleneck ratio, shared group width, and monotonic width/depth constraints) down to RegNet, a low-dimensional space of simple regular networks whose per-block widths follow a quantized linear function of depth.

Finds design principles that contradict common practice: the best models have stable depth (~20 blocks) across compute regimes, use bottleneck ratio b=1 (i.e., no bottleneck), and widths/group-width increase with model complexity.

Introduces RegNetX (plain) and RegNetY (RegNetX + Squeeze-and-Excitation) model families spanning 200MF-32GF, including the specific RegNetY-400MF configuration (Fig. 16 / Table of top RegNetY models: 0.4 GF, 3.9M params, 4.3M acts, 25.9% top-1 error) our paper's backbone is drawn from.

Shows RegNet models are competitive with or faster than ResNe(X)t and EfficientNet under comparable, carefully controlled training settings (up to 5x faster on GPUs at matched accuracy), and that the design-space ranking generalizes across flop regimes, epoch counts, stage counts, and to ImageNetV2.
Releases code/pretrained models (pycls) that are the standard source for RegNetY checkpoints used downstream.
our_use: main.tex:347-349, 'The headline grid uses three backbones, MobileNetV3 \citep{howard2019searching}, RegNetY-400MF \citep{radosavovic2020designing}, and a ViT-B/16 transformer \citep{dosovitskiy2021image}, to show the findings are not CNN-specific.' -- cited purely as the origin/definition of the RegNetY-400MF backbone architecture used in the multi-backbone robustness check.
